name: PA-09
label: Safe R

key_factors: Strong Republican district lean of R+19
Incumbent Dan Meuser running for reelection with a large fundraising edge
Prediction markets price Democratic chances at about 3%
No polling or expert ratings available
model.rationale: The district's R+19 lean, Meuser's incumbency, and his roughly three-to-one fundraising advantage over Rachel Wallace all point to a comfortable Republican hold, and Polymarket prices a Democratic win at only about 3%. With no polls or expert ratings to the contrary, the fundamentals-based margin stands essentially unchanged.
model.watch: A major scandal, unexpected incumbent retirement, or a dramatic late spending surge by Wallace could narrow the race.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Dan Meuser seeks another term in a northeastern Pennsylvania district that leans heavily Republican, about nineteen points toward the GOP at the partisan baseline. He enters the general election with a clear financial edge, having raised roughly $1.9 million to Rachel Wallace's $700,000, and holds more cash despite heavier primary spending. Wallace, a first-time challenger, has no outside support on record and no polling exists in the race.

Prediction markets give Wallace only about a three percent chance of an upset, and no expert raters have flagged the contest as competitive. The fundamentals point to a solid Republican win in the mid-to-high teens, with modest uncertainty given the absence of survey data. Barring an unforeseen development, Meuser is strongly favored to hold the seat.
